narration_timeline.text: Why do these horses spend so much time with their heads down in the grass?
narration_timeline.scene: Real close horse grazing on a California meadow.

narration_timeline.text: Some horses accept food from a person, while others keep grazing along the water's edge.
narration_timeline.scene: A real Icelandic horse is hand-fed by a person, then a different Camargue horse grazes at a lakeside. Do not imply hand-feeding is grazing.

narration_timeline.text: In other pastures, groups walk together, pause, and lower their heads again.
narration_timeline.scene: Two real Camargue horse clips from the same Slovenian nature area.

narration_timeline.text: Horses are grazing animals, built to take in forage over many parts of the day.
narration_timeline.scene: Another genuine Camargue horse grazing/walking view.

narration_timeline.text: Between mouthfuls, they keep an eye on other horses sharing their own fields.
narration_timeline.scene: Camargue horses in a different spring meadow.

narration_timeline.text: The quiet routine continues near water and trees: move with the group, then lower the head to graze.
narration_timeline.scene: Actual Camargue horses standing together at a lake and a different white horse grazing on a wooded path.
